name: Question 20
problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X∼N(4,{\sigma }^{2})$ is a normal random variable with $P(2<X<6)=0.2812,$ find ${\sigma }^{2},$ rounded to $2$ decimal places.

| $z$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ | $\,0.07\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.3\,$ | $\,0.6368\,$ | $\,0.6406\,$ | $\,0.6443\,$ |
| $\,0.4\,$ | $\,0.6736\,$ | $\,0.6772\,$ | $\,0.6808\,$ |
| $\,0.5\,$ | $\,0.7088\,$ | $\,0.7123\,$ | $\,0.7157\,$ |

*Hint: Note that the interval $2<X<6$ is symmetric about the mean $\mu =4.$*

${\sigma }^{2}≈$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
First, we find the cumulative probability using symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(2<X<6) & =0.2812 \\ 2P(4<X<6) & =0.2812 \\ P(4<X<6) & =0.1406 \\ P(X<6)-P(X<4) & =0.1406 \\ P(X<6)-0.5 & =0.1406 \\ P(X<6) & =0.6406 \\ P(X\le 6) & =0.6406\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 6) & =0.6406 \\ P(Z\le \frac{6-4}{\sigma }) & =0.6406 \\ Φ(\frac{2}{\sigma }) & =0.6406 \\ \frac{2}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.6406)\end{aligned}
$$

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(0.36)=0.6406\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(0.6406)=0.36.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sigma } & =0.36 \\ \sigma  & =\frac{2}{0.36} \\ \sigma  & ≈5.555\,56.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2}=(5.555\,56)^{2}≈30.86\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.
